source_text: Observational studies, including randomized trials in high-HIV-prevalence regions, demonstrate that the foreskin increases heterosexual HIV acquisition risk by enriching target cells (e.g., Langerhans cells) in its inner mucosa, with circumcision conferring 50-60% relative protection against infection; however, these findings derive largely from African cohorts and may attenuate in low-prevalence settings with condom use. [87] [88]
